migration.description: Add persistent task identity colors, execution and deferral timelines, observation coverage, and bounded per-run workload samples to the maintenance SQLite database.
migration.release_unit_description: Task operations API, durable run workload observations, recent-100 overlapping detail charts, and Retention's seven-day backlog view.

durable_state.description: Managed task controls and stable colors, progress snapshots, legacy task-run history, actual execution timestamps, execution and deferral intervals, observation sessions, explicit coverage gaps, and per-task run workload samples.
durable_state.storage_implementation: Sibling SQLite file derived from DATABASE_PATH or MAINTENANCE_DATABASE_PATH.

ddl_structural_changes.description: Create managed task, progress, and run tables in the maintenance database and add execution UID, actual start/end/duration, and fixed task-color columns idempotently.
Create indexed execution, deferral, coverage-session, and maintenance-revision tables; existing request-time and duration columns keep their prior meanings.

Create the maintenance-store workload sample table and task-attempt index with execution UID plus task key identity, monotonic sequence, status, and serialized per-metric coverage; add the status column idempotently when upgrading an earlier table shape.

dml_changes.description: Seed the stable task registry and measurement capabilities idempotently, assign deterministic colors only where a color is missing, and preserve existing enablement and schedule overrides.

historical_data_backfill_or_transformati.description: Retain the existing idempotent compatibility copy for legacy task runs and startup-backfill state.
Not applicable: legacy request timestamps and cumulative durations cannot prove actual execution boundaries, so no historical execution intervals are inferred.
Do not backfill metric values. Confirmed legacy managed attempts may be merged by stable identity at read time, but their missing P/D/C values and actual-start uncertainty remain unknown.

progress_signals: stable registry, capability, and color counts
workload sample count and per-task latest-100 retention
pause_points: after stable task-color and capability assignment
after each legacy compatibility copy batch

required_test_evidence: candidate opens fresh and prior maintenance schemas and seeds stable task colors without replacing control values
restarting after a partial copy is idempotent and does not duplicate runs
maintenance database unavailability and dropped observations create explicit coverage gaps without writing task observations to the main database
legacy request-time and duration fields retain their prior meanings and no historical execution start is inferred
legacy task API remains readable while additive runtime, timeline, measurement-capability, and workload-trend fields are available
the workload table migration is idempotent, rejects stale sample sequences, protects each task's latest 100 samples and running sample, and does not reconstruct old P/D/C metrics
legacy managed attempts deduplicate against new samples by execution identity while their historical metric values remain unknown
